{{Short description|German physicist}}
'''Gerhard Haerendel''' is a German space scientist.

==Life and career==
Born in 1935, Haerendel obtained his PhD in [[physics]] from [[LMU Munich]] in 1963.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpe.mpg.de/7587514/haerendel-gerhard|title=Haerendel, Gerhard|website=www.mpe.mpg.de}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.iafastro.org/biographie/gerhard-haerendel.html|title=IAF : Gerhard HAERENDEL|first=International Astronautical|last=Federation|website=www.iafastro.org}}</ref>

He was elected as a Fellow to the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics and Astrophysics]] in 1969.<ref name="auto"></ref><ref name="auto2"></ref>

He became the director of the Max Planck Institute for Physics and Astrophysics in 1972, and retired in 2000.<ref name="auto"></ref><ref name="auto2"></ref>

==Awards==
* Fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]]<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/m/haerendel-gerhard|title=ÖAW Mitglieder Detail|website=www.oeaw.ac.at}}</ref>
* Jean Dominique Cassini Medal of the [[European Geosciences Union]]<ref name="auto1"></ref>
* Space Science Award of the Committee on Space Research<ref name="auto1"></ref>
* Van Allen Medal<ref name="auto1"></ref>
* Von Karman Award by the [[International Academy of Astronautics]]<ref name="auto1"></ref>
